text:
The snapshot looks like late 2009. Unemployment is 9.4%, which matches roughly May 2009. Headline CPI at -1.89% YoY is close to the July 2009 trough of about -2.1%, though June 2009 was about -1.4%. Industrial production at -13% YoY also fits mid-2009.

Several details help pin the month:
- Fed funds at 0.14% and a 10-year yield of 3.46% are consistent with mid-2009.
- US equities returned +48% over 6 months, which means the window starts at the March 2009 low. The 12-month return of -18.3% fits a June–July window.
- The 3-month return of +8.6% is consistent with the S&P gaining from about 890 at end-March to about 919 at end-June, or from end-April to end-July.
- VIX at 24.76 fits end-June 2009 (about 26) or end-July (about 25).
- Unemployment of 9.4% was the May reading (released in June). June was 9.5%, so the latest value is May and the snapshot is end of June 2009.
- Headline CPI for May 2009 was -1.28%, while the June figure was -1.43% and July's was -2.1%. A reading of -1.89 is not an exact match, but the data may be differently defined.
- Core CPI at 1.56% fits roughly mid-2009.

Checking the equity returns against July 2009: the 1-month return was +7.4%, which does not match the +3.7% here. June 2009 returned about +0.2%, which doesn't match either. Looking at August 2009, the 1-month return was +3.7%, the 6-month return from end-February (735) to end-August (1020) was +39%, and the 12-month return was about -18%. That fits better, with unemployment at 9.4% for July (the August release would show 9.6% for August, so July's 9.4% fits as the latest value). July's headline CPI was -2.1%, near the -1.89 shown. So the snapshot is end of August 2009.
